To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
n-3 PUFAs and curcumin synergistically target aberrant Wnt and NF-κb signaling in Lgr 5+ stem cells and induce targeted apoptosis in damaged Lgr5 +stem cells to reduce colon carcinogenesis.

n-3 PUFAs and curcumin synergize to increase targeted apoptosis in DNA damaged Lgr5 + stem cells in the colon, and that this effect is mediated by upregulation of the p53 signaling pathway in these cells.
dietary bioactives synergistically enhance p53-mediated apoptosis and suppress Wnt signaling in Lgr 5+ stem cells following the induction of colon carcinogenesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of dietary bioactive agents, n-3 PUFAs and curcumin, on colon cancer initiation in the context of intestinal stem cells.
the role of diet in the initiation and progression of colorectal cancer.
the effects of dietary bioactive agents, n-3 PUFAs and polyphenols on Lgr5-positive stem cells in the colon, which are the cells of origin for colon cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dietary n-3 PUFAs and curcumin synergistically target aberrant Lgr5+ intestinal stem cells to reduce the initiation and progression of colon cancer in a mouse model.
dietary n-3 PUFAs and polyphenols synergistically target Lgr5+ colon stem cells to reduce tumor initiation.
n-3 PUFAs and polyphenols are synergistic in their ability to reduce colon cancer risk by targeting DNA-damaged LGR5+ stem cells, and this effect may be due to p53 signaling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the n-6/n-3 PUFA ratio and curcumin are important dietary factors that can be used in the prevention or therapy of colon cancer.
the combination of n-3 PUFAs and curcumin synergistically reduced the incidence of colon cancer by targeting the cells of origin, Lgr5-positive stem cells.

n-3 PUFAs and curcumin are synergistically more effective than either agent alone in reducing the number of DNA-damaged LGR5+ stem cells, and that the combination of the dietary bioactive agents is more effective than either alone in preventing colon tumor progression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dietary polyphenols and PUFAs may be used in combination to reduce colon cancer risk, particularly when administered at the time of DNA damage.
n-3 PUFAs in combination with polyphenols synergistically target Lgr5+ intestinal stem cells for elimination during tumor initiation.
the combination of n-3 fatty acids and polyphenols can be used to prevent colon cancer initiation by eliminating damaged stem cells.
